architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence, with the controlling contribution of reactive-core dilution versus modifier-specific suppression unresolved.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C thermal-hold measurements show a 15-60 min relative viscosity change of 9.51% for E1 versus 51.54% for E5, establishing substantial formulation-dependent isothermal drift.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local hold data contain only four time points over 15-90 min and only one original run for E1 and one for E5; they do not provide the matched 15-60 min repeat measurements needed to distinguish linear dilution from superlinear suppression or tackifier-specific effects. By comparison, temperature response has six points from 80-130 C, although its realization spread is large.
measurement_requirements: Measure a matched 120 C isothermal hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report SI_15_60 as the primary observable.
Run at least two independent preparations or repeats with fully recorded process history so drift can be compared against realization variability.
Compare the observed matched-window drift with the frozen reactive-core linear-dilution prediction at the same reactive mass fraction.
Include a composition contrast that distinguishes acrylic-like modification from activation of the minor tackifier-like axis, without changing the comparison window or measurement protocol.
Keep all measurements within the supported 120 C and 15-60 min domain and report realized viscosity levels separately from the time-dependent drift.
planner.scientific_question: At a matched reactive-mass fraction and within the measured temperature/time domain, does adding modifier produce thermal-hold drift substantially below the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction, and is low drift obtained only when the minor tackifier-like axis is active rather than with the acrylic-like axis alone? This separates H-CORE from H-RESIN and H-DUAL.

hypotheses_not_separated: H-CORE versus H-DUAL cannot be fully separated if the outcome is near the linear-dilution prediction, because both predict near-linear behavior for an acrylic-only composition without a minor tackifier arm.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is below half the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction, 0.5 x (9.51% x 0.85) = 4.04%, this establishes superlinear suppression for the supported 15% acrylic-only intervention, supports H-RESIN, and falsifies the acrylic-only near-linear prediction of H-DUAL as well as H-CORE.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above the linear-dilution prediction, 9.51% x 0.85 = 8.08%, H-RESIN is falsified for this composition; the result supports reactive-core dilution behavior and is compatible with H-CORE and the acrylic-only branch of H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between 4.04% and 8.08% is below linear dilution but not sufficiently below half the prediction to support H-RESIN under the registered criterion; it leaves the mechanism unresolved and requires a matched tackifier-active contrast.

proposer.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured directly at 120 C over the 15-60 min matched window

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: The 15% acrylic plus 2.5% minor-tackifier composition is inside the supported regions and could test combined mitigation, but a single dual-axis result cannot establish that the minor tackifier is required because it lacks an acrylic-only comparator.
The temperature-response descriptor is regression-derived, addresses a less unresolved coordinate, and does not directly measure the declared thermal-hold failure mode.
Repeatability directly characterizes process-state spread but does not discriminate the registered formulation-mechanism hypotheses.

proposer.reasoning: This card directly measures the least-resolved coordinate using the matched 120 C hold window and requires independent repeats. The 15% acrylic loading lies within the externally supported intervention region and preserves the E2 reactive-core proportions, while its reactive mass fraction of 0.85 gives a clear linear prediction of 8.08%. The registered half-linear threshold provides an interpretable test of superlinear suppression. An acrylic-only arm is also the most informative single composition for challenging H-DUAL, because low drift would directly contradict the prediction that acrylic addition alone remains near linear.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace the 15% acrylic-only S1C39 hold with the unmodified E2-derived reactive-core control. This establishes the contemporaneous matched-window baseline needed to interpret any subsequent modifier effect; it does not by itself resolve H-DUAL.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: Cannot be determined because the deterministic ranking, tied top set, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, and recommendation_flip_boundary were withheld. The proposal is therefore not demonstrably inside the deterministic top set.
residual_decision_risk: The E2 control alone does not distinguish H-CORE from H-DUAL; a minor-tackifier-only arm is still required.
The large E2 realization spread may obscure drift differences unless process history and independent repeats are tightly controlled.
The repeat-level rule for classifying results near the 4.04% and 8.08% thresholds remains unspecified.
The withheld deterministic ranking and perturbation sweep prevent an assessment of top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, or recommendation_flip_boundary.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is decisive for experiment selection: S1C39 uses an E1-derived drift coefficient as the baseline for an E2-derived reactive core, so a deviation from 8.08% cannot be attributed uniquely to the acrylic-like modifier. The immediate experiment should therefore be the unmodified E2-core matched-window hold under the same 120 C, 15-60 min, independent-repeat protocol. This changes which experiment should be run, not merely how S1C39 would be interpreted. A minor-tackifier-only arm remains needed later to separate H-CORE from the acrylic-only branch of H-DUAL.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No weight perturbation results were supplied, so no defensible perturbation boundary can be identified. Weight sensitivity is unavailable rather than evidence of robustness.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: SI_15_60 is a directly measured matched-window quantity at 120 C, and a value at or above 8.08% can be produced by the stated protocol. However, the criterion is scientifically interpretable only after measuring the unmodified E2-derived core under the same hold protocol; otherwise the E1-based reference transfer is an uncontrolled assumption.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A near-linear result could not identify reactive-core dilution as opposed to the acrylic-only branch of H-DUAL, and it could not establish that the minor tackifier is required.
objections.objection: The proposed experiment S1C39::M-HOLD-120 contains only the 15% acrylic-only arm. If SI_15_60 is at or above the linear prediction of 8.08%, H-CORE and the acrylic-only branch of H-DUAL remain observationally entangled, while H-DUAL's requirement for a minor-tackifier-active arm is not tested. The proposer admits only the H-CORE versus H-DUAL entanglement, but the claimed separation list still overstates what one arm can establish.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result below 8.08% could be attributed to acrylic-like superlinear suppression even if it instead reflects the different reactive-core composition or stoichiometric state of E2 relative to E1.
objections.objection: The linear-dilution reference for S1C39 is calculated as 9.51% from original formulation E1 multiplied by phi_r = 0.85. The candidate preserves the E2 reactive-core proportions, but no matched 120 C hold of unmodified E2 is included. E1 and E2 are distinct original formulations, so any difference between the E1 drift coefficient and the E2-core drift coefficient is confounded with the alleged acrylic suppression.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment would support only deviation from an assumed E1-based dilution calculation, not causal attribution to the acrylic axis.
objections.objection: The candidate changes total composition by 15% acrylic-like modifier and reduces reactive mass fraction to 0.85. Although this is the intended contrast for H-CORE, the experiment has no unmodified E2 control measured with the same 120 C, 15-60 min protocol, so modifier effects cannot be separated from the unmeasured baseline drift of the actual E2-derived core.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The stated support and falsification decisions could depend on an unstated averaging or rounding rule rather than the registered measurement resolution.
objections.objection: The registered H-RESIN support threshold is SI_15_60 below half the linear prediction, 4.04%, whereas the measurement catalog declares a 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold. The 4.04% separation from the 8.08% linear prediction exceeds 2 percentage points, so the nominal thresholds are separable, but the two-repeat protocol does not specify how repeat-level variation will be combined or how a result straddling 4.04% or 8.08% will be classified.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A nominal H-RESIN falsification would not reliably falsify resin modification; it could instead expose failure of the E1-to-E2 baseline transfer.
objections.objection: The falsification criterion for H-RESIN is SI_15_60 at or above 8.08%, but 8.08% is an E1-derived single-run reference rather than a contemporaneous matched-window estimate for the E2-derived core. M-HOLD-120 directly measures the candidate SI_15_60, yet the protocol does not measure the control needed to determine whether an observed value at or above 8.08% is a modifier result or baseline-transfer error.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could be reported as evidence for a formulation-level suppression pattern, but not as confirmation of the stated concentration or encounter-frequency mechanism.
objections.objection: The proposer says that a low result 'establishes superlinear suppression' and attributes it to effective concentration and encounter frequency. The registry permits formulation-level rheological adjudication, but M-HOLD-120 alone cannot establish that particular mechanistic explanation; it only tests the registered drift prediction.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add an unmodified E2-core control measured at 120 C for 15, 30, 45 and 60 min with the same independent-repeat protocol, and use that control's matched-window drift as the frozen linear-dilution baseline. To adjudicate H-DUAL rather than merely challenge it, also add a minor-tackifier-only arm at a registered nonzero loading, such as 2.5% or 5%, with the same protocol.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The linear-dilution reference for S1C39 is calculated from original formulation E1, while the 15% acrylic candidate preserves the E2 reactive-core proportions and no matched unmodified E2 hold is measured. Therefore a deviation from 8.08% is not uniquely attributable to acrylic-like suppression.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.
